sub_theme: The Wright Brothers and the History of Flight

lessons.title: Story Time: Dreaming of Flight
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to discuss a character's determination to achieve a dream.
success_criteria: I can say what the character wanted.
I can say how they worked towards it.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss what it would have been like before flight existed.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Read a story/biography extract about the Wright brothers' dream of flight, modelling discussion of determination.
lessons.independent_task: Children discuss and record the Wright brothers' dream and how they worked towards it.
key_questions: What did they want to achieve?
How did they work towards it?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note comprehension of determination/achievement theme — evidence for ENG.R2.
lessons.home_link: Tell your family about the Wright brothers.

lessons.title: Measuring Distance: How Far Did the First Flight Go?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to compare distances using standard units in a historical context.
success_criteria: I can measure a distance.
I can compare it to a known distance.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss the distance of the first Wright brothers' flight (about 37 metres) and model measuring this distance practically if possible.
lessons.independent_task: Children measure out and compare the first flight's distance to other known distances (e.g. the classroom length).
key_questions: How does this distance compare to our classroom?
Is that far for a first flight?

differentiation.greater_depth: Compare to multiple other known distances

lessons.assessment_notes: Note practical measuring applied to a historical fact — evidence for MATHS.MEA.
lessons.plenary: Recap how far the first flight went.
lessons.home_link: Measure a similar distance at home or in your garden.

lessons.title: Who Were the Wright Brothers?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to recall key facts about the Wright brothers' achievement.
success_criteria: I can say who the Wright brothers were.
I can say what they achieved.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at a picture of an early aeroplane.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Introduce the Wright brothers and their achievement of the first powered flight in 1903.
lessons.independent_task: Children record key facts about the Wright brothers in a fact file.
key_questions: When did they achieve first flight?
What was special about their achievement?

differentiation.support: Complete fact file with word bank

lessons.assessment_notes: Note recall of a significant historical achievement — evidence for HIST.1.
lessons.home_link: Tell your family what you learned about the Wright brothers.

lessons.title: Writing About the First Flight
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to write factual sentences about the first flight using the past tense.
success_criteria: I can write a fact about the first flight.
I can use the past tense consistently.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap facts about the Wright brothers from Monday.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model writing a factual sentence about the first flight using consistent past tense.
lessons.independent_task: Children write 2-3 factual sentences about the first flight.
key_questions: What fact will you write?
Is your sentence in the past tense?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note factual writing with tense consistency — evidence for ENG.W2/W3.
lessons.home_link: Tell your family a fact about the first flight.

lessons.title: Timeline of Flight: A Chart
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to represent key flight milestones on a simple timeline chart.
success_criteria: I can place events on a timeline.
I can say what happened when.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model creating a timeline chart of key flight milestones (first flight 1903, first transatlantic flight, first commercial flights).
lessons.independent_task: Children create a timeline chart of flight milestones, answering questions about it.
key_questions: What happened first?
How much time passed between these events?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note chronological data representation, a cross-curricular skill — evidence for MATHS.STAT/HIST.1.
lessons.home_link: Create a timeline of something else with your family.

lessons.title: How Have Aeroplanes Changed?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe how aeroplanes have changed since the Wright brothers' time.
success_criteria: I can describe an early aeroplane.
I can compare it to a modern one.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at pictures of early and modern aeroplanes.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss how aeroplanes have changed (size, speed, materials, passenger capacity) since 1903.
lessons.independent_task: Children compare an early and modern aeroplane, recording changes noticed.
resources_needed: Early and modern aeroplane picture cards
key_questions: What is different about this early aeroplane?
How have modern aeroplanes improved?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note change over time understanding linked to a significant achievement — evidence for HIST.1.
lessons.home_link: Look at pictures of old and new aeroplanes together.

lessons.title: Phonics: Reading Flight Words
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to blend and read flight-themed words.
success_criteria: I can read flight words.
I can read a sentence about flight.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Reinforce a spelling pattern, applying it to flight-themed words (e.g. 'wing', 'engine', 'sky').
lessons.independent_task: Children read themed word and sentence cards.
key_questions: Can you read this word?
Can you read this sentence?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note phonics/spelling application — evidence for ENG.R1.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate reading progress with a themed reading game.
lessons.home_link: Practise reading flight words over the week.

lessons.title: Shapes of Aeroplanes
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to identify 2D and 3D shapes within an aeroplane design.
success_criteria: I can name a shape in an aeroplane.
I can describe its properties.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss shapes found in aeroplane design (cylindrical fuselage, triangular/rectangular wings).
lessons.independent_task: Children identify and label shapes in an aeroplane diagram.
key_questions: What shape is the fuselage?
What shape are the wings?

differentiation.greater_depth: Identify multiple shapes and describe properties

lessons.assessment_notes: Note shape recognition applied to a design context — evidence for MATHS.GEO.
lessons.home_link: Look at the shapes in a toy plane or picture at home.

lessons.title: Other Flight Pioneers
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to recall a fact about another significant flight pioneer.
success_criteria: I can name another flight pioneer.
I can say what they achieved.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Introduce another flight pioneer (e.g. Amelia Earhart, revisiting/extending Year 1 learning with more depth).
lessons.independent_task: Children record a fact about another flight pioneer in their fact file.
key_questions: What did this pioneer achieve?
Why was it significant?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note recall of a second significant individual related to flight — evidence for HIST.1.
lessons.home_link: Tell your family about another flight pioneer.

lessons.title: Hot-Seating a Wright Brother
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to answer questions in role as a Wright brother.
success_criteria: I can answer a question in role.
I can use facts I've learned.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap facts about the Wright brothers learned this week.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model hot-seating as a Wright brother, answering questions using known facts.
lessons.independent_task: Children take turns hot-seating as a Wright brother, answering classmates' questions.
key_questions: Why did you want to build a flying machine?
What was your first flight like?

differentiation.greater_depth: Answer unprompted, in character, with detail

lessons.assessment_notes: Note spoken language and factual recall in role — evidence for ENG.SL1/HIST.1.
lessons.home_link: Pretend to be a Wright brother and tell your family about your achievement.

lessons.title: Flight Word Problems
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to solve addition/subtraction word problems using a flight context.
success_criteria: I can solve an addition problem.
I can solve a subtraction problem.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap addition and subtraction strategies to 100.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model solving word problems using a flight context (e.g. passengers on a plane).
lessons.independent_task: Children solve flight-themed word problems within 100, showing working.
key_questions: How many altogether?
How many are left?
lessons.assessment_notes: Record word problem solving skill — evidence for MATHS.N2.
lessons.home_link: Make up a flight word problem for your family.

lessons.title: Why Is the Wright Brothers' Achievement Still Celebrated?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to explain why the first flight is still celebrated today.
success_criteria: I can say why it's still celebrated.
I can name something it led to.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss the Wright brothers' legacy — leading to modern air travel connecting the world.
lessons.independent_task: Children record why the Wright brothers' achievement is still celebrated and its legacy.
key_questions: What did their achievement lead to?
Why do we still remember them?

differentiation.greater_depth: Give detailed reasoning about the achievement's lasting impact

lessons.assessment_notes: Note understanding of historical legacy and significance — evidence for HIST.1.
lessons.home_link: Talk about a time your family travelled by plane, if applicable.

lessons.title: The Wright Brothers Quiz: Reading Comprehension
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to answer comprehension questions about the Wright brothers and flight.
success_criteria: I can answer a retrieval question.
I can answer an inference question.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the week's learning about the Wright brothers.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Read a summary passage about the Wright brothers, modelling retrieval and inference questions.
lessons.independent_task: Children answer a mix of retrieval and inference questions about the passage.
key_questions: What did the Wright brothers achieve?
Why was persistence important to their success?

differentiation.support: Answer retrieval questions with text pointing

lessons.assessment_notes: Note comprehension progress — evidence for ENG.R2.
lessons.home_link: Quiz your family on Wright brothers facts.

lessons.title: Maths Review: Measuring, Shape, Timeline Data
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to apply measuring, shape and data skills learned this week.
success_criteria: I can measure distance.
I can name shapes.
I can read a timeline chart.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Quick recap of the week's measuring, shape, and data learning.
lessons.independent_task: Children rotate through 3 stations covering each skill.
key_questions: How far is this?
What shape is this?
What does the timeline show?
lessons.assessment_notes: Summarise week 24 maths observations for each child — evidence for MATHS.MEA/GEO/STAT.
lessons.plenary: Class recap game combining all three skills.
lessons.home_link: Continue practising measuring over the weekend.

lessons.title: The Wright Brothers and Flight Topic Recap
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to summarise key facts about the Wright brothers and the history of flight.
success_criteria: I can say what the Wright brothers achieved.
I can say how flight has changed since then.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss synthesising the week's learning about the Wright brothers and flight.
lessons.independent_task: Contribute to a class 'History of Flight' display combining fact files, timelines, and hot-seat notes from the week.
key_questions: What have we learned about the history of flight?
What was most interesting?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note synthesis of the week's learning on a significant historical achievement — evidence for HIST.1.
lessons.plenary: Unveil the finished 'History of Flight' display.
lessons.home_link: Share what you learned about the history of flight with your family.
